summary.intent: Close a race in addrConn's connection-establishment path: hold ac.mu continuously from the Idle/state check in connect()/updateAddrs() through the transition to Connecting inside the renamed resetTransportAndUnlock(), so two goroutines can no longer both observe Idle and both start a parallel connection attempt (orphaning one transport). Motivated by a ~0.4% flake in Test/AuthorityRevive traced to this exact race (issue grpc/grpc-go#7365).
summary.issue_fit: Full — the root cause and fix described in issue grpc/grpc-go#7365's comments (hold the lock through the state transition) match the shipped diff exactly, and the requested doc comment (dfawley, review thread on commit 6214c9d) was added verbatim.
summary.coverage: Complete: the only changed file, clientconn.go, was read in full diff and function context at base and head; every call site of resetTransportAndUnlock in the repository was located (connect(), updateAddrs(), no others) and traced through every branch for lock balance. `go build .` and `go vet .` pass at head. Focused subtests most related to this path (UpdateAddresses_NoopIfCalledWithSameAddresses, ResetConnectBackoff, BackoffCancel, Dial_OneBackoffPerRetryGroup) pass under -race. The previously flaky xds/internal/xdsclient/tests Test/AuthorityRevive passes 30/30 under -race.

observations.fact: No regression test was added for the fixed race itself; the author instead verified manually that Test/AuthorityRevive stopped flaking over 100000 local attempts (PR body, "Tested" section), a scale this review could not reproduce.
observations.evidence: Diff manifest: clientconn.go only, no *_test.go changes; pr-body/"Verified that Test/AuthorityRevive no longer flakes for 100000 attempts with the change."

requirements.source: pr-body/"client: fix race that could lead to orphaned connections and associated resources."
requirements.evidence: clientconn.go:922 and :996 now call resetTransportAndUnlock() while still holding ac.mu from connect()'s/updateAddrs()'s Idle-state check; resetTransportAndUnlock (clientconn.go:1234-1262) transitions state to Connecting before releasing the lock, closing the window in which a second concurrent caller could also observe Idle. Verified by fresh-context verifier: premise-race-closed ruling=holds.

requirements.source: pr-body/"caller of resetTransport() keep holding the mutex instead of releasing it and having resetTransport() re-acquire it"
requirements.evidence: clientconn.go:905-923 (connect) and :940-996 (updateAddrs) no longer call ac.mu.Unlock() before invoking resetTransportAndUnlock; the renamed function's doc comment (clientconn.go:1231-1233) states the lock must be held by the caller and it guarantees release. Verified by fresh-context verifier: premise-lock-discipline ruling=holds.

requirements.source: issue-grpc/grpc-go#7365/"A simple fix it to set the state to connecting while addrConn.connect has the mutex locked"
requirements.evidence: clientconn.go:1261-1262: ac.updateConnectivityState(connectivity.Connecting, nil) happens immediately before ac.mu.Unlock(), i.e. while the caller's lock acquisition is still held, matching the described fix approach.

requirements.source: pr-body/"Verified that Test/AuthorityRevive no longer flakes for 100000 attempts with the change."
requirements.evidence: This review's execution allowance (5 minutes/command, offline) cannot reproduce a 100000-iteration run. Reviewer ran the test 30 times under -race instead (all passed), which is consistent with but does not establish the claimed ~0.4%-flake elimination at that scale.
clientconn.go:1231-1233 carries exactly the doc comment dfawley requested in review ("ac.mu must be held by the caller, and this function will guarantee it is released.").
